content: 1. Patients should be monitored for signs of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis when using letermovir. 2. When letermovir is co-administered with cyclosporine, the dose of pravastatin should not exceed 20 mg orally once daily. 3. Pretomanid increases the levels or effects of letermovir through mechanisms involving other pathways. Use caution and monitor for drug-related adverse effects. 4. Increased monitoring is recommended when pretomanid is co-administered with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. 5. Letermovir increases the levels of micronized progesterone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Letermovir increases the levels of natural progesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 7. Letermovir increases the levels of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 8. Letermovir enhances the effects of propranolol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Letermovir increases the levels of quetiapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 10. Letermovir increases the levels of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 11. Letermovir increases the levels of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 12. Letermovir increases the levels of rabeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Letermovir increases the levels of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Letermovir increases the levels of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 15. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 16. Letermovir increases the levels of rifaximin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 17. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid repeating the rimegepant dose within 48 hours if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 18. Letermovir increases the levels of risperidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Ritonavir increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Letermovir increases the levels of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Letermovir increases the levels of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 22. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of rosiglitazone through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Monitor glucose concentrations. 23. Letermovir increases the levels of rosuvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Co-administration of letermovir with fluvastatin may require a dosage reduction. Monitor patients closely for myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. 25. When letermovir is co-administered with cyclosporine, the dose of rosuvastatin should not exceed 5 mg orally once daily. 26. Letermovir increases the levels of salmeterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 27. Letermovir increases the levels of saxagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Letermovir increases the levels of seladelpar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Exercise caution in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers taking seladelpar and co-administered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 29. Letermovir increases the levels of sertraline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 30. Letermovir increases the levels of sildenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Letermovir increases the levels of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Monitor sirolimus plasma concentrations during treatment and after discontinuation of letermovir, and adjust the sirolimus dose accordingly. When letermovir is co-administered with cyclosporine, sirolimus should be taken 4 hours after cyclosporine oral administration. Higher doses of sirolimus may be needed to maintain recommended trough concentration ranges if cyclosporine is discontinued from combination therapy. 32. Letermovir increases the levels of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 33. Letermovir increases the levels of sorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 34. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of sparsentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. No dosage adjustment is needed. Monitor blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function regularly if sparsentan is co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 35. Letermovir increases the levels of sufentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 36. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of sufentanil SL by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Co-administration of sufentanil SL with any CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, potentially leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including fatal respiratory depression. 37. Letermovir increases the levels of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 38. Tacrolimus increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 39. Letermovir increases the levels of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Monitor tacrolimus plasma concentrations during treatment and after discontinuation of letermovir, and adjust the tacrolimus dose accordingly. 40. Letermovir increases the levels of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 41. Letermovir increases the levels of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 42. Telmisartan increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 43. Letermovir increases the levels of telmisartan through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor. Letermovir, as an OATP1B1/3 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of co-administered OATP1B1/3 substrates. 44. Teriflunomide increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Co-administration of letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may increase letermovir plasma concentrations. 45. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of letermovir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 46. Ublituximab decreases the effects of letermovir through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor. 47. Valsartan increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 48. Letermovir increases the levels of valsartan through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor. Letermovir, as an OATP1B1/3 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of co-administered OATP1B1/3 substrates. 49. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with drugs associated with nephrotoxicity may increase the risk for acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity. 50. Letermovir decreases the levels or effects of voriconazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Closely monitor for reduced effectiveness of voriconazole. 51. Voxilaprevir increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Co-administration of letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may increase letermovir plasma concentrations. 52. Letermovir increases the levels of zaleplon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 53. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce zanubrutinib (a CYP3A4 substrate) to 80 mg orally twice daily when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Interrupt the dose as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous dose of zanubrutinib. 54. Letermovir increases the levels of zileuton by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 55. Letermovir increases the levels of ziprasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 56. Letermovir increases the levels of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 57. Letermovir and entecavir may increase each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Co-administration with drugs that reduce renal function or compete for active tubular secretion may increase serum concentrations of either entecavir or the co-administered drug. 58. Voclosporin increases the levels or effects of letermovir through other mechanisms. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Information suggests that voclosporin (an OATP1B1 inhibitor) may increase the concentration of OATP1B1 substrates. Monitor for adverse reactions of OATP1B1 substrates when co-administered with voclosporin. 59. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of acarbose through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Monitor glucose concentrations. 60. Letermovir increases the levels of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 61. Letermovir increases the levels of alfuzosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 62. Letermovir increases the levels of aliskiren by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 63. Letermovir increases the levels of almotriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 64. Letermovir increases the levels of alprazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 65. Letermovir increases the levels of ambrisentan through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor. Letermovir, as an OATP1B1/3 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of co-administered OATP1B1/3 substrates. 66. Letermovir increases the levels of amiodarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Close monitoring for increased amiodarone effects and concentrations is recommended when concomitantly used with letermovir. 67. Letermovir increases the levels of amitriptyline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 68. Letermovir increases the levels of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 69. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of letermovir by increasing its elimination. Use caution and monitor. 70. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of letermovir through other mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 71. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of letermovir by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of letermovir with P-gp inducers is not recommended. 72. Letermovir increases the levels of aprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 73. Letermovir increases the levels of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 74. Letermovir increases the levels of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 75. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 76. Atorvastatin increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 77. Letermovir increases the levels of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Co-administration with atorvastatin and letermovir should not exceed an atorvastatin dosage of 20 mg daily. Monitor patients closely for myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. When letermovir is co-administered with cyclosporine, the use of atorvastatin is not recommended. 78. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of avapritinib with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unable to avoid, reduce the avapritinib starting dose. See the drug monograph for dosage modifications. 79. Berotralstat increases the levels or effects of letermovir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Monitor or titrate the P-gp substrate dose if co-administered. 80. Letermovir increases the levels of bexarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 81. Letermovir increases the levels of bosentan through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor. Letermovir, as an OATP1B1/3 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of co-administered OATP1B1/3 substrates. 82. Letermovir increases the levels of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 83. Letermovir increases the levels of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 84. Letermovir increases the levels of buprenorphine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 85. Letermovir increases the levels of buspirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 86. Letermovir increases the levels of caffeine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 87. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of canagliflozin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Monitor glucose concentrations. 88. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered.
